solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scale WW2 bomber

definitions.meaning: the Bristol ... was a British torpedo bomber of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A note about the size or rating of a wartime bomber aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the same surname: a wind-force scale and a Bristol aircraft type.

clue.text: Takes a break without Dad at customs

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the letters for Dad from the longer word

parts.note: to take a break is to pause, so this phrase gives the verb form pauses
Pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone stops for a rest at the customs desk while their father is elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customs' looks like the border post but is the definition in the sense of habits or practices.
explanation.definitionFit: Uses and customs are both established practices or habits, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: So, endless fretting — upset?

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the trimmed word upside down, reading it backwards
endless means the final letter of the word for fretting is cut off

parts.note: fretting is worry

explanation.surface: A sympathetic question: so, after all that ceaseless fretting, are you upset?
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' does double duty: in this down clue it turns the trimmed word upside down, and it also colours the whole clue, which reads as its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief brought on by endless fretting and distress is a fair description of sadness or woe.

clue.text: Fat cats are male relatives of father's side

parts.note: agnates are relatives descended through the male line

explanation.surface: A remark that the wealthy elite are all the men on one family's paternal side.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat cats are wealthy, powerful businesspeople, the same as tycoons.

clue.text: Express of distinct parts

definitions.meaning: to express something is to put it clearly into words
an ... structure is jointed, made of separate segments

explanation.surface: It reads like a description of a train with separate carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to voice clearly; the adjective in biology means jointed or segmented.

clue.text: New fruit, not peeled first for city

indicators.note: not tells us the following letter is left out of the fruit

parts.note: apples are a fruit

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word peeled

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's instruction about fresh fruit that should not be peeled for city customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not peeled first' removes P, the first letter of 'peeled', from APPLES to leave APLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a major city in southern Italy.

clue.text: Some worn-out place for hacks

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: It suggests a shabby, worn-out office where journalists work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn-out' looks like one adjective, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on SOME WORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacks are journalists, and the office where news is gathered and written is where they work.

clue.text: Voodoo priestess shed tail, because of snakes

indicators.note: shed tail means the final letter of the priestess's title is dropped

parts.note: a mambo is a priestess in Haitian voodoo
as can mean because

explanation.surface: A voodoo priestess lost her tail because of snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed tail' cuts the last letter from MAMBO to give MAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Mambas are venomous African serpents, so the plural noun fits the definition exactly.

clue.text: One boy embracing jolly pilot

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: embracing means the boy's name wraps round the next piece

parts.note: Ian is a boy's name
a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A lad hugging a cheerful flier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective but is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is an aviator, a member of an air force, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Birds and whales broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so we want a word sounding like the whales

parts.note: orcs is an old word for whales such as killer whales

explanation.surface: A wildlife programme about seabirds and whales going out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Auks are diving seabirds of northern waters, such as puffins and guillemots.

clue.text: Broke molar around block in old building

indicators.note: around means the scrambled tooth letters go round the block
broke means smashed, so the letters of molar are rearranged

parts.note: an anvil is a heavy iron block used by smiths

explanation.surface: Someone cracked a molar on a block inside an ancient building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' looks like a past tense in the story but is the anagram signal; the scrambled tooth splits either side of the smith's block.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman villa is an ancient country house from the Roman era, an old building.

clue.text: Second barge at capital

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
a scow is a flat-bottomed barge

explanation.surface: A short moment spent on a barge in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital city of Russia.

clue.text: High standard way to cook red bun. Cool!

indicators.note: a way to cook something is to mix it up, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A baking tip on how to cook a red bun, with a cheerful exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about cookery, which fits the answer's other sense of top-class cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes first-rate cooking or anything of the top quality.

clue.text: Benevolence the French reject — that's commonplace

indicators.note: reject means throw back, so the French article is turned round

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a truism is a commonplace statement

explanation.surface: A claim that the French spurn kindness as something trite.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfless concern for the welfare of others is goodwill, a synonym of kindness.

clue.text: Perplexed cast

definitions.meaning: cast is the past participle of throw, as in a stone hurled

explanation.surface: A baffled actor among the cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disconcerted is being put off balance; a hurled object has been tossed.

clue.text: Prize money first won at the crease?

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word won

parts.note: in cricket the batsman at the crease is having an innings, a turn at batting

explanation.surface: A cricket bonus earned by a batsman's first triumph at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the marked line where the batsman stands, and an innings is a turn at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Money gained from a successful bet or contest is the cash a victor collects.

clue.text: Land for cultivation in Maine, say?

parts.note: Maine is an example of an eastern US state, giving E for eastern
Maine is one of the United States, so it is an example of a state

explanation.surface: A question about farmland in a New England state.
explanation.walkthrough: Maine is in the north-east of the USA, so it is an E(astern) STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tract of land owned and farmed, often with a house, is a landed property.

clue.text: King Edward the First got up, turning into trouble

indicators.note: the First picks the opening letter of the name Edward
in a down clue got up means the word for king is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rex is Latin for king

indicators.note: turning means the letters of the word into are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale of King Edward I rising and turning into a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' reverses REX to XER; 'turning' rearranges INTO as TION.
explanation.definitionFit: To take trouble over something is to put in effort, a synonym of strenuous exertion.

clue.text: Inappropriately mention tedious chore at university

parts.note: a drag is a tiresome task
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone tactlessly complains about a boring task while at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an embarrassing subject from the past unnecessarily is to bring it back up.

clue.text: Glass boat

definitions.meaning: a large drinking glass for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with two or more masts

explanation.surface: It could describe a glass-bottomed boat.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a tall drinking vessel and a fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel.

clue.text: Prisoner following a bishop for short chat

parts.note: a con is a convict
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An inmate trailing after a bishop in search of a quick word.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word is a shortening of confabulation, an informal talk or chinwag.

clue.text: Notes timeless commissions

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: brevets are military commissions giving an officer a higher rank

explanation.surface: Memos about officers' promotions that never go out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Breves are long musical notes, each worth two semibreves.

clue.text: Hit the sack first — that's pandemonium

indicators.note: first tells us the bed piece comes before the beating word

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
to lam is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Advice to go to bed early because there is chaos around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit the sack' reads as a phrase for going to bed, but 'Hit' is LAM and 'the sack' is BED, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after a London asylum, means uproar and chaos.

clue.text: Disturbed guard in bed — full length

indicators.note: disturbed means shaken up, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sentry woken in bed while lying at full stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A book not cut down is complete, printed at its whole extent.

clue.text: Spoken of extravagant skirt

indicators.note: spoken of means said out loud, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: too-too is a dated word meaning excessive or affected

explanation.surface: Gossip about a showy, over-the-top skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt worn by a ballerina.

clue.text: Mrs T. can, at first

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word at

explanation.surface: A boast that Mrs T. can do it at the first attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mrs T.' looks like Mrs Thatcher but is a definition by example: Tina Turner.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer Tina Turner is one woman whose surname begins with T.

clue.text: Untrustworthy chap greeted horse, we're told

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, as in bade good morning

indicators.note: we're told means the horse word is heard as two spoken letters

parts.note: gee-gee is childish slang for a horse

explanation.surface: A rogue hailed a horse, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the nursery word for a horse is just the letter G twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotten person is idiomatically a bad egg.

clue.text: Ordinary old coin in change?

parts.note: plain means ordinary
a bob was a pre-decimal British shilling

explanation.surface: An everyday old coin given in change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' is not money but bell-ringing: Plain Bob is a basic method of change ringing on church bells, and a bob was a British shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: In bell-ringing a change is a sequence of bells, and this is a standard method of ringing them.
